QEngine v1.0 vs vLLM 0.28 on RTX 3090s

Serving benchmark of a custom C++/CUDA inference engine (QEngine) against vLLM, on the same Qwen3.8-27B INT4 checkpoint, the same OpenAI-compatible chat API and the same benchmark client (vllm bench serve), with identical prompts and seeds for every engine. Measured 21–22 October 2026.

Model: Qwen3.8-27B INT4 (same checkpoint) QEngine: 3× RTX 3090, tensor parallel 3 vLLM: 2× RTX 3090, tensor parallel 2Client: vllm bench serve 0.28.0
QEngine v1.0 (1be10df, 2026-10-21) QEngine v0.1 (1c3f603, 2026-10-18) vLLM 0.28 (best config)

Throughput vs concurrency

Where vLLM is ahead

Every point where a vLLM variant beat QEngine v1.0 on a median latency metric. At RAG c=8 vLLM's chunked prefill interleaves the 15K-token prefills with decoding: the first token arrives sooner (12.3 s vs 22.3 s), but each following token takes 115–165 ms instead of 9.6 ms. The other three are 4–19% margins. Cells: TTFT p50 (ms) / TPOT p50 (ms).

Methodology

Engines

  • QEngine v1.0: master 1be10df (2026-10-21). QEngine v0.1: master 1c3f603 (2026-10-18). Both on 3× RTX 3090 with tensor parallel 3, 32 sequences, 262,144 context, built-in MTP head (adaptive, up to 7 draft tokens).
  • vLLM 0.28 (best config): vLLM 0.28.0 with the community club-3090 “qwen3.8-27b dual-fast” recipe, ported flag for flag, plus the two club-3090 runtime patches that fix MTP crashes under concurrency (FlashInfer decode-plan pinned-buffer race; GDN + MTP async spec-decode ordering). W4A8 Marlin, fp8 KV cache, prefix caching, chunked prefill, 32 sequences, 262,144 context. Measured twice: with MTP speculative decoding (4 draft tokens) and without; every chart uses, per point, the better of the two (named in each chart's footnote and table). vLLM 0.28.0 is the newest release that builds with this host's toolchain.
  • GPU count. vLLM runs on 2 GPUs, QEngine on 3. Tensor parallel 3 is not possible in vLLM for this model: its 4 KV heads and 16 DeltaNet key heads are not divisible by 3. TP=2 is the strongest vLLM layout available on this machine and the one the community recipe uses. All numbers are whole-system throughput and latency, not per GPU.

Client and workloads

  • vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions, sampling sent explicitly (--temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --top-k 20), thinking off. --ignore-eos on synthetic datasets (fixed output length); ShareGPT uses its real lengths. Each point has its own seed, identical across engines, so no point reuses another's prompts. A short unsaved warm-up precedes every point. Engines ran one at a time, each on a freshly started server.
  • Classic: --max-concurrency C --request-rate inf, C ∈ {1, 8, 16, 32}. short = 1024 in / 512 out; agent = 500 / 2000; rag16k = 15000 / 128 (c=1, 8); ShareGPT V3 first user turns.
  • Goodput: Poisson arrivals (--request-rate R --burstiness 1.0), no client concurrency cap. SLA: TTFT ≤ 3000 ms and TPOT ≤ 50 ms per request (--goodput ttft:3000 tpot:50). chat = 1024 shared + 1024 unique / 256 out, 180 s of arrivals per rate; long16k = 12288 + 4096 / 512, 240 s; agent = 4096 + 2048 / 1024, 240 s; lengths vary ±50%.
  • Prefill: one unique prompt, --random-output-len 1 --max-concurrency 1, lengths 1K–200K, 1 warm-up + 3 measured runs with different seeds (no prefix-cache hits); median TTFT reported. TTFT is measured client-side.
  • TPOT follows the vLLM definition: (end-to-end latency − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1), per request; medians shown.

Stability check

At the end of the session, short c=1 and c=32 were repeated on a freshly started server for every engine with the same prompts. All engines reproduced within ±5% at c=1 and ±2.2% at c=32 (QEngine v1.0: −2.6% / +0.3%).

Caveats

  • One failed request in the whole run: vLLM MTP, goodput chat at 1 req/s (179 of 180 completed, client-side disconnect, server stayed up). The no-spec variant is the vLLM best at that point.
  • QEngine v1.0 is slightly slower than v0.1 on short chat at c=1 (208 vs 218 tok/s, reproduced in the stability check) and faster at every other point.
  • vLLM best in goodput is chosen by goodput req/s, so at agent 0.25 req/s it is the MTP run (0.230 req/s, 97% in SLA) although no-spec had 100% in SLA at 0.228 req/s.
  • Different GPU counts (3 vs 2), see above.
